primary_texts.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 5.111 Principles of Chemical Science, Fall 2008, Lecture Summary 6
primary_texts.locator: Printed lecture pages 1 and 3-5; sections The Physical Interpretation of a Wavefunction and Radial Probability Distribution.
primary_texts.observed_content: Defines squared wavefunction as probability density per unit volume; separately defines radial probability in a thin spherical shell. Identifies the most probable radius of hydrogen 1s as the Bohr radius and rejects well-defined electron orbits. The energy-level discussion relates emitted or absorbed radiation to transitions between levels.
primary_texts.qualification: This is a lecture handout with some blanks and formulas absent from the text extraction. Only readable text was used; no missing material was guessed from pixels.

primary_texts.title: The Development of the Space-Time View of Quantum Electrodynamics
primary_texts.author: Richard P. Feynman
primary_texts.locator: Opening autobiographical discussion, beginning with the paragraph about eight years of work and publication in 1947.
primary_texts.short_excerpt: the quantum theory of electricity and magnetism was not completely satisfactory.
primary_texts.observed_content: Feynman describes unresolved quantum electromagnetic theory during his undergraduate study and subsequent work through the 1940s. This independently contradicts any claim that the full satisfactory construction was finished in the 1920s.
primary_texts.qualification: The terminal output was truncated in the middle of the long lecture. The opening passage used here was fully visible; no truncated passage was used.

primary_texts.title: Development of Quantum Electrodynamics: Personal recollections
primary_texts.author: Sin-Itiro Tomonaga
primary_texts.locator: Opening section (1), reference 2, end of section (2), and section (6).
short_excerpts: Heisenberg and Pauli, Z. Physik, 56 (1929) I.
I began this work about 1942, and completed it in 1946.
primary_texts.observed_content: Tomonaga describes the early Heisenberg-Pauli field theory as applying Hamiltonian quantum mechanics, with its cited paper dated 1929. He then describes later covariant formulation and the postwar resolution of divergent calculations. This supports a quantum-mechanical framework already present in the 1920s and early QED development then, without claiming later completion occurred then.
primary_texts.qualification: A formal early framework is not the same as the later satisfactory perturbative theory. No exact first-invention date is inferred; the reviewed lesson claims only the decade.
